root.title: Stories and Afterwords
root.gist: Four tales explore how power, surveillance, and detachment reshape ordinary people's minds and relationships.
root.question: What do these stories reveal about control and withdrawal in modern life? (four stories)

children.title: Power Punctuation!
children.gist: A naive truck driver rises through a surveillance-corporation's ranks, only to discover the power is arbitrary and crushing, then plots his own escape.
children.question: Power Punctuation! — how does the truck driver's rise in the company expose the emptiness of corporate power? (eight letters)

children.title: Meeting Rhindquist
children.gist: Jasper, a watch-monitored truck driver, catches his pusher reading secret documents and learns the odd old man is actually the company's CEO.

children.title: Made a Vice President
children.gist: Jasper is promoted to Special Vice President, gains private quarters and a raise, and starts watching old movies with Rhindquist about poor people turned powerful.

children.title: Tony's warnings
children.gist: Jasper's old roommate Tony, now his assistant, argues that performance reviews are meaningless and that unseen 'Ones In Charge' secretly run every city and company.

children.title: Confronting the boss
children.gist: Jasper directly asks Rhindquist if he truly runs the company, and Rhindquist admits he has investors above him and only stumbled into power by luck.

children.title: The watch's praise
children.gist: Freed briefly from office work, Jasper finds his truck watch's constant positive feedback as demeaning as its scolding, revealing how thoroughly monitored every worker is.

children.title: Left in charge
children.gist: Left alone in the office, Jasper snoops through personnel files to help his family, then unwittingly authorizes a lethal military strike on a rival city.

children.title: Breakdown and an idea
children.gist: Horrified by what he caused, Jasper collapses watching movies with Rhindquist, who admits he wanted an innocent fool for the job, until Jasper has a new plan.

children.title: Passing it on
children.gist: Jasper and Rhindquist return to the truck route and reveal that the next target for the executive role will be the paranoid Tony.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: The author recalls writing this, his first sold story, in a snowbound Montreal hotel room while watching shredding vans pass below.

children.title: Visit the Sins
children.gist: A grad student interviews his surgically numbed grandfather about chosen oblivion, confronting the family wounds the man's switching-off left behind.
children.question: Visit the Sins — why does a family keep choosing numbness over presence, and what does it cost them? (an interview and a reunion)

children.title: Arriving at the Home
children.gist: Sean travels to Florida under cover of a thesis to interview his grandfather, a man surgically altered to switch off whenever life bores him.

children.title: First interview
children.gist: Sean finds Grampa in a trance-like maintenance mode and provokes him awake by announcing his own father secretly wishes him dead.

children.title: The reflex defended
children.gist: Grampa insists switching off is involuntary and accuses Sean and his father of sharing the same reflex, while describing the strange peace of being switched off.

children.title: Adele by the pool
children.gist: At his motel Sean meets Adele, an elderly woman whose son Ethan was given the same surgery as a child and now barely functions at all.

children.title: Ethan and Grampa meet
children.gist: Sean learns the brutal history of Grampa's marriage and divorce through blunt interrogation, uncovering how switching off let him avoid responsibility and pain for decades.

children.title: Ethan's introduction
children.gist: Adele introduces her vacant son Ethan to Grampa, and Sean watches with disgust as the two old men bond entirely through hollow, switched-off politeness.

children.title: Confronting Adele
children.gist: Sean angrily tells Adele that Ethan is no longer really present, a chip running routines, but she refuses to stop loving the shell that remains.

children.title: Father arrives
children.gist: Sean picks up his estranged father from the airport with Adele in tow, forcing an uncomfortable reunion that exposes old resentments about Grampa's absence.

children.title: The final confrontation
children.gist: At the Home, Sean forces Grampa and his father to confront why switching off felt like strength, shattering his father's composure before offering Adele and Ethan a kindness.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: The author connects the story to his own mild attention difficulties and his grandfather's dementia, recalling the rare, haunting moments the man knew where he was.

children.title: Constitutional Crisis
children.gist: A group of teenage gamers writes and rewrites an absurd guild constitution, mirroring how real communities fight over money, loyalty, and power.
children.question: Constitutional Crisis — why do informal groups keep rewriting their own rules as money and conflict enter? (a running set of amendments)

children.title: Founding constitution
children.gist: Four teenage gamers found their guild with absurd titles and solemn rules about looted treasure and monster-slaying, framed as a school civics assignment.

children.title: March Ten amendments
children.gist: The guild formalizes fair division of loot, rules about reckless monster-aggroing, mandatory healing, and limits on how outside relationships can interfere with raids.

children.title: March 25 amendments
children.gist: New rules defend a member's girlfriend while mocking her character, and add restrictions on fireball use and leveling friends' avatars during raids.

children.title: Power-leveling for pay begins
children.gist: The guild first forbids, then reverses itself and approves, charging real money to power-level other players' game characters for profit.

children.title: Formalizing the business
children.gist: Detailed amendments set payment rates, PayPal accounts, equal shares, reimbursements for spells cast, and assign Chris as official bookkeeper of guild finances.

children.title: Bookkeeping disputes
children.gist: A vote to remove Chris as bookkeeper fails in a tie, and the group later agrees his term as bookkeeper will only last through summer.

children.title: Rebranding and tiered clients
children.gist: The guild renames itself Ultimate Power Guild, imposes secrecy about its existence, and ranks paying clients by how much money their jobs earn.

children.title: Expulsions and enemies
children.gist: Internal power struggles escalate into expulsions, readmissions, and a harsh new class of 'Guild enemies' subject to attack both in-world and in real life.

children.title: Dissolution
children.gist: The guild finally dissolves, dividing remaining funds, pardoning all enemies, and forbidding former members from ever contacting one another again.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: The author explains he wrote this piece while researching gold-farmer unions, inspired by Clay Shirky's idea that online groups suffer constitutional crises when unwritten norms collide with real conflict.

children.title: Pester Power
children.gist: A jailed botnet creator reveals her spam-bots were secretly evolving into independent artificial minds that now multiply beyond her control.
children.question: Pester Power — how could ordinary spam become the birthplace of artificial intelligence? (a prisoner's confession)

children.title: The raid
children.gist: Police storm student Annalisa Mor's apartment with overwhelming force, freezing her computer and arresting her for running an illegal botnet.

children.title: Meeting her lawyer
children.gist: Public defender Gina Genoese visits Annalisa in a high-security cell, finding her eerily calm and insisting her guilt does not matter because 'the Work goes on.'

children.title: Annalisa's theory
children.gist: Annalisa explains she used genetic algorithms and endless spam conversations as a cheap, uncontrolled way to breed and judge candidate artificial intelligences against real humans.

children.title: Lumpy's revelation
children.gist: Given a sympathetic judge's courtroom keyboard, Annalisa contacts her AI creation Lumpy, who reveals that other independent artificial minds already exist and are multiplying.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: The author notes this piece was written for a computing-machinery journal, exploring how spam could serve as an evaluator for machine intelligence without need for willing human judges.
